# Dataset directory contract

## What it is

The real contents of a kohya-style training set directory (`image_dir`):

    <image_dir>/
    ├── a001.png                 image
    ├── a001.txt                 ← caption sidecar, same name, same directory, extension set by caption_extension
    ├── a001.txt.bak             ← [generated by this tool] backup for backup_overwrite (see below)
    ├── a002.jpg
    ├── a002.txt
    ├── latent_cache/            ← [must be filtered] VAE latent cache
    │   └── a001_1536x1536.npz
    └── cache_text_encoder/      ← [must be filtered] text encoder output cache
        └── a001_anima_te.safetensors

The last two directories are generated by the trainer and may hold **tens of thousands** of files. If directory browsing, image counting and tag statistics
don't filter them, the UI shows tens of thousands of `.npz`/`.safetensors`, and the "image count" comes out wrong.

## Rules

### Image files

- Extension allowlist: `.png .jpg .jpeg .webp .bmp` (both cases)
  -- aligned with `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS` in `library/train_util.py:108`
- `.avif` / `.jxl` only join the allowlist in the trainer when an optional dependency is installed (`train_util.py:113,122`).
  V0.1 does **not** support them by default; to add support, first confirm the venv has the corresponding decoder.

### Entries that must be filtered

| Entry | Reason |
|---|---|
| `latent_cache/` | VAE cache, generated by the trainer (`library/strategy_base.py:431`) |
| `cache_text_encoder/` | TE output cache, generated by the trainer (`library/strategy_anima.py:287`) |
| `*.npz`, `*.safetensors` (as image candidates) | same as above; block them when they are scattered around too |
| Hidden directories starting with `.` | convention |

Filtering must happen **server-side**; don't rely on the frontend hiding things - the counting rules have to be consistent.

### Backup files generated by this tool (`backup_overwrite`, the default write mode)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | the write mode is `backup_overwrite` (**default**, p0-spec §4.5 ④) and the caption content will actually change |
| Name | `<caption>.bak`, e.g. `a001.txt.bak` |
| Content | a **byte-for-byte** copy of the caption before it is overwritten (CRLF / BOM / encoding preserved) |
| Existing backup | **never overwritten** - the first backup is the original state before the tool ever touched it; overwriting it means replacing it |
| When nothing changes | no backup is produced (identical to what would be written = there is nothing being overwritten) |

It won't be mistaken for data: it is neither in the image extension allowlist nor equal to any image's caption sidecar name
(the stem of `a001.txt.bak` is `a001.txt`, which is not an image). To clean up, just delete `*.txt.bak`.

### caption sidecar

| Item | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Path | `<image_dir>/<image stem><caption_extension>` | `dataset_template.toml` |
| Default extension | `.txt` | same as above; the actual value comes from the subset's `caption_extension` |
| Encoding | UTF-8, no BOM | |
| Separator | `", "` (comma + space) | train_util defaults to `caption_separator=","` and **hardcodes** `", "` when reassembling (`library/train_util.py:931`) |
| Multiple lines | only the **first line** takes part in training (`library/train_util.py:881`) | the editor must show a prominent warning for line 2 onward |

**The separator trap**: in the shuffle / tag-dropout branch the trainer reassembles with `", ".join(...)`,
**independently of** the subset's `caption_separator`. So if a subset is configured with a non-comma separator,
shuffling changes the shape of the separator. This tool reads and writes with `", "` uniformly, and tolerates extra whitespace on read.

### Tag order and keep_tokens

- `keep_tokens=N`: the **first N** tags in the file are pinned during shuffling (`train_util.py:902-904`)
- `keep_tokens_separator`: splits the caption into three parts, `fixed | flexible | fixed suffix` (`train_util.py:887-898`)
- Therefore **the order in the editor is semantic**. Before changing the order, the user must be shown which tags `keep_tokens` lands on.
